title: Testing Inter-Universe Particle Transitions in a Particle Accelerator
content: We propose a laboratory test of particle conversion between the visible sector of our universe and orthogonal external quantum sectors within a tiered-multiverse framework. Our universe occupies tier n=30, while the destination states are calibrated to electron-energy eigenvalues associated with tiers 29 and 31. Tier-dependent values of c and ℏ, combined with four-momentum conservation, produce two independent predictions. In the 30→29 absorption channel, a tagged electron leaves the visible sector after absorbing a photon with rest-frame invariant energy 10.427131 keV. The laboratory resonance shifts with electron velocity and collision angle. In the pump-assisted 30→31 channel, electron transfer is accompanied by a signal photon constrained by the invariant scale 10.018278 keV. An equal-gap pump produces signal energies of 19.28-20.04 keV, whereas an 8 keV pump produces 17.47-18.02 keV and removes the exact two-Compton-photon pileup degeneracy. Because the gateway couplings are phenomenological and unknown, the model predicts the resonance manifolds but not unique event probabilities. We propose a tagged-electron hard-X-ray free-electron-laser experiment using electron spectroscopy, photon detection, charge collection, and hermetic vetoes. Conservative illustrative 5σ probability sensitivities range from 3.27×10-7  for 109 electrons to 1.03×10-8 for 1012 electrons. A positive result must reproduce the moving resonances and complete event topologies. A null result would constrain both effective gateway interactions.
